questions.q: What is the primary reason for ensuring regular cleaning of a house?
options: To make the house look beautiful
To prevent it from becoming a breeding ground for insects and diseases
To rearrange furniture frequently for a new look
To make it inviting for guests

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Match Column A (cleaning agents) with Column B (articles). A: (a) Brick powder (b) Tamarind pulp (c) Newspaper (d) Mild detergent. B: (i) Glass (ii) Linoleum (iii) Brass (iv) Iron.
Match the methods of cleaning with the procedures. A: (i) Mopping (ii) Dusting (iii) Polishing. B: (a) Wipe with dry cloth (b) Rub to bring shine (c) Wipe with wet cloth.
Specify the role of the following in cleaning: lemon, ammonia, methylated spirit, sand.
questions.answer: Lemon cleans stains from brass and copper. Ammonia is a grease emulsifier. Methylated spirit is a grease solvent. Sand is an abrasive for hard surfaces.

questions.q: True or False. (a) Mops should be washed and dried after use. (b) Strong acids should be left on tiles overnight.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: acids must be rinsed off quickly.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why is a damp cloth recommended for mopping instead of a very wet one?
questions.answer: A damp cloth removes dust and dirt without spreading excess water. Too much water leaves the floor slippery and wet and can damage the floor.

questions.q: What four points would you adopt while using a dustbin?
questions.answer: Use a plastic bin with a lid, line it with paper or a polythene bag, empty it daily, and wash and dry it regularly.

questions.q: Differentiate between dust and dirt.
questions.answer: Dust is loose particles that settle on surfaces and are removed with a dry cloth. Dirt is dust that sticks with moisture or grease and needs detergent.

questions.q: Name any two cleaning equipments and their use.
questions.answer: A mop is used to wipe floors with a damp cloth. A dust pan collects the swept dust to be thrown in the dustbin.

questions.q: State two principles to be followed while using polishes.
questions.answer: Remove dust and dirt thoroughly before polishing and use small quantities. Rub off the polish thoroughly so the surface is not sticky.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the steps to clean a room daily (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Open the windows, remove unwanted articles and empty ash trays and dust bins. (ii) Sweep, dust furniture and brush or vacuum the carpet. (iii) Mop the floor, replace linen and survey the room.

questions.q: Explain the cleaning materials used for cleaning (any three) with their uses.
questions.answer: (i) Detergents with water clean most surfaces. (ii) Abrasives such as sand and emery paper scrub hard dirt. (iii) Alkalis like baking soda emulsify grease and solvents like methylated spirit dissolve grease and wax.

questions.q: Distinguish between daily, weekly and spring cleaning.
questions.answer: (i) Daily cleaning is a general cleaning of open surfaces. (ii) Weekly cleaning is more thorough and includes drawers, fittings and stains. (iii) Spring cleaning is the most thorough annual cleaning with removal of furniture and curtains and polishing.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the six methods of cleaning with the equipment used.
questions.answer: (i) Dusting with a clean soft duster. (ii) Shaking and beating carpets and curtains in open air. (iii) Sweeping with a soft broom and collecting dust in a dust pan. (iv) Mopping with a damp mop. (v) Washing with a yard broom, water and detergent. (vi) Polishing with polish and a flannel cloth to get a shine.
